This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review, prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261385134), synthesizes randomized controlled trial evidence for both plants across eight mental health outcomes, with the literature search updated to 31 August 2026. From 494 initial records, 452 remained after duplicate removal; 34 studies met eligibility criteria (19 saffron, 14 ashwagandha, 1 comprehensive review), comprising 31 randomized controlled trials. Saffron demonstrated efficacy for depression (10 randomized controlled trials [RCTs]), anxiety (9 RCTs), and sleep (8 RCTs) at 15-30 mg/day standardized extract. Ashwagandha showed efficacy for anxiety (10 RCTs), stress (8 RCTs), and sleep (3 RCTs) at 30-600 mg/day with a withanolide-standardized extract, with a pooled cortisol reduction of -3.27 µg/dL. Risk of bias was low in 10 of 31 trials and raised some concerns in most of the remainder, and GRADE certainty was moderate at best. Both plants exhibited favorable safety profiles, although ashwagandha-associated hepatotoxicity warrants liver enzyme monitoring during prolonged use. Critically, no RCTs exist for burnout or posttraumatic stress disorder in either plant, despite mechanistic evidence of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis normalization, reduced neuroinflammation, and monoaminergic and gamma-aminobutyric acid-ergic modulation; this evidence is predominantly preclinical and requires clinical confirmation. This systematic review identifies these conditions as priority targets for well-designed clinical trials. The bioactive constituents-crocin and safranal in saffron, and withanolides in ashwagandha-share overlapping mechanistic pathways highly relevant to these underserved, high-burden disorders.

papers.title: High-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation improves sleep quality in patients with mild Alzheimer's disease: Findings from the TRANSFORM-AD study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundHigh-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS) has shown beneficial effects on cognitive function in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, data on the effects of hi-tACS on sleep quality and emotional state in patients with AD are still limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the influences of hi-tACS on sleep quality and emotional state in AD.MethodsThe TRANSFORM-AD study was a double-blind, randomized-controlled trial that enrolled individuals with mild AD. Participants were randomized to receive hi-tACS group or sham stimulation group, and underwent 30 one-hour sessions of either 40 Hz tACS or sham stimulation over consecutive 15 consecutive days. Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI), Hamilton anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Hamilton depression Rating Scale (HAMD) and Quality of life in Alzheimer's Disease scale (QOL-AD) were evaluated at baseline, and the end of the intervention.ResultsAmong 43 participants with complete baseline and post-intervention assessments, Hi-tACS reduced post-intervention PSQI scores compared with sham after adjustment for baseline PSQI (adjusted mean difference, -2.34 points; 95% CI, -3.63 to -1.05; p < 0.001). Baseline-adjusted effects for HAMA (-1.43; 95% CI, -2.89 to 0.02), HAMD (0.44; 95% CI, -1.28 to 2.15), and QOL-AD (2.07; 95% CI, -1.57 to 5.70) were imprecise and included the null.ConclusionHi-tACS improved subjective sleep quality in patients with mild AD. The present secondary analysis did not provide conclusive evidence of effects on anxiety, depression, or quality of life; these exploratory outcomes require confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.Trial registration:ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03920826.

papers.title: Emotional State Evolution and Nursing Interventions in Patients Undergoing HSCT in Laminar Airflow Clean Rooms: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is an established treatment for hematologic and other serious disorders, but the transplantation process can impose substantial psychological burdens. Protective isolation in laminar airflow clean rooms restricts social contact while patients simultaneously experience intensive conditioning, treatment-related symptoms, uncertainty, and dependence on professional care. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the evolution of emotional states across the HSCT trajectory, factors associated with psychological distress, assessment approaches, and nursing strategies. Relevant literature was searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, CINAHL, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data from database inception to August 31, 2026. Available evidence suggests that emotional responses vary across treatment phases and patient groups rather than following a uniform trajectory. Anxiety and uncertainty may be more prominent before transplantation and during entry into protective isolation, whereas depressive symptoms and broader distress may increase during myelosuppression and prolonged isolation. Psychological distress is associated with environmental isolation, physical symptom burden, information-related uncertainty, limitations in social and family support, treatment-related neuropsychiatric effects of corticosteroids, and inflammatory signaling. Nurses can contribute through repeated assessment, symptom management, communication and psychoeducation, support for family and social contact, sleep and relaxation strategies, and timely referral to specialist services. Empirical support varies across interventions, with stronger evidence for selected approaches such as inpatient palliative care and emerging evidence for educational, relaxation, digital, and recreational interventions. Future research should prioritize standardized assessment, longitudinal multicenter designs, and phase-specific individualized supportive care.

papers.title: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the Traditional Chinese NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) for assessing perceived workload in Taiwanese adults.
papers.abstract: BackgroundPerceived workload is central to occupational health, ergonomics, and rehabilitation research, yet no guideline-based Traditional Chinese version of the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) has been available for Taiwan and other Traditional-Chinese-speaking settings.ObjectiveTo cross-culturally adapt the NASA-TLX into Traditional Chinese (NASA-TLX-TC) and evaluate its measurement properties in Taiwanese adults.MethodsIn a psychometric secondary analysis, 114 community-dwelling adults aged 20-50 years completed the NASA-TLX-TC on three consecutive days. Within the COSMIN framework, we examined content validity, internal consistency, structural validity (exploratory factor analysis with parallel analysis), test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation [ICC]), measurement error, and construct validity (seven a priori hypotheses involving sleep, mood, and shift work).ResultsThe content validity index averaged 0.88 and Cronbach's α was 0.83. The six dimensions loaded on a single factor (55.8% of variance). The three-day average score showed good reliability (ICC[A,k] = 0.83), whereas single-day reliability was moderate (0.62); the minimal detectable change was 32 points. Six of seven construct-validity hypotheses were supported; the shift-work difference was in the predicted direction but nonsignificant. Internal consistency and convergent validity were stable across subgroups.ConclusionsThe NASA-TLX-TC showed good reliability and initial construct validity and is suitable for group-level occupational-health, ergonomics, and rehabilitation research; multi-day averaging is recommended for individual assessment.

papers.title: The cognitive cost of artificial intelligence on ageing workforce: Analyzing age-related effects on mental workload and task performance in computer-based environment.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe current world demographic reality necessitates a critical re-evaluation of how technological tools, specifically those powered by artificial intelligence (AI), interact with the varying cognitive profiles of a ageing workforce.ObjectivesThe objective of this study is to evaluate the spatial distribution of mental workload and objective task performance across AI-assisted and non-AI-assisted conditions in a computer-based environment.MethodAn experimental study involving 30 older workers compared standardized office tasks under non-AI-assisted (Segment A) and AI-assisted (Segment B) conditions. Mental workload was assessed using NASA-TLX, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), and EEG-based Beta-Alpha Ratios (BAR) across frontal (F3, F4), parietal (P3, P4), and occipital (O1, O2) regions. Performance in document preparation (Task 1) and arithmetic operations (Task 2) was evaluated using percentage-based accuracy, efficiency, and overall performance scores.ResultAI intervention improved overall task performance but was accompanied by an apparent performance-workload paradox, whereby enhanced output coincided with increased neurophysiological and systemic strain. Descriptively, NASA-TLX Overall Perceived Workload decreased from 54.05 to 44.91 during complex tasks, while HRV declined by 48.68% in Task 1, indicating acute autonomic strain. EEG revealed increased BAR in the frontal (F3: 29.2%), parietal (P3), and occipital (O1) regions, suggesting heightened attentional and sensory demands associated with monitoring and verifying AI-generated suggestions.ConclusionAI redistributes rather than eliminates workload, increasing executive verification and visual monitoring demands. Future AI systems for older adults should prioritize cognitive ergonomics to minimize executive burden and sensory strain, preventing premature cognitive fatigue while enhancing task performance and supporting sustainable human-AI interaction.

papers.title: Combined Effect of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry on Cardiovascular Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)-chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap syndrome has been linked to worse cardiovascular outcomes. Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) is recognized as an early stage of chronic obstructive pulmonary diseas. However, whether the coexistence of OSA and PRISm confers increased cardiovascular risk remains unknown. Using data from the Sleep Heart Health Study, participants were categorized into 4 groups according to OSA and PRISm status. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. The secondary outcome was cardiovascular disease mortality. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to evaluate the association of these groups with the risk of cardiovascular outcomes. During a median follow-up of 11.45 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events was 17.00% in non-OSA with normal lung function, 27.52% in non-OSA with PRISm, 25.28% in OSA with normal lung function, and 49.40% in OSA with PRISm. After multivariable adjustment, compared with non-OSA with normal lung function, the adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events were 1.20 (95% CI, 0.82-1.75) in non-OSA with PRISm, 1.04 (95% CI, 0.89-1.21) in OSA with normal lung function, and 1.52 (95% CI, 1.08-2.12) in OSA with PRISm. Corresponding HRs for CVD mortality were 2.02 (95% CI, 1.26-3.24), 1.05 (95% CI, 0.81-1.35), and 2.17 (95% CI, 1.41-3.34), respectively. A significant sex interaction was observed (P for interaction=0.009), with the association present only in women. The coexistence of OSA and PRISm is independently associated with increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This association is observed predominantly in women.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Sedentary Behavior, Physical Activity, and Sleep During Pregnancy and Offspring Health: Protocol for the Pregnancy 24/7 Offspring Multi-Site Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Childhood obesity is a major public health concern that increases cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease theory posits that obesity and CVD risk is, in part, programmed in utero. A greater understanding of modifiable maternal factors that associate with offspring obesity and CVD risk in childhood could inform primordial prevention interventions during pregnancy. Maternal sedentary behavior, physical activity, and sleep during pregnancy are modifiable and plausible determinants of offspring obesity and CVD risk yet remain insufficiently studied. This protocol describes the design of the Pregnancy 24/7 Offspring Study (NCT07172880), developed to address this gap in knowledge. This study examines associations between device-based maternal 24-hour movement behavior (sedentary behavior, physical activity, and sleep) measured in each pregnancy trimester and analyzed via trajectories and as compositions with offspring obesity and CVD risk through 24 months of age. Maternal 24-hour movement behavior data and birth outcomes were previously collected in the Pregnancy 24/7 Cohort Study (N=500, Iowa, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia). The Offspring study extends this cohort by enrolling up to 450 maternal-offspring dyads and collecting new measures in the offspring, including body mass index z-score from birth through 24 months obtained via medical record abstraction, anthropometry, indicators of CVD risk, and maternal questionnaires. The primary outcome is body mass index z-score trajectory; secondary outcomes include adiposity, blood pressure, and brachial-femoral pulse wave velocity. Findings from this study will advance understanding of how maternal 24-hour activity associates with early-life obesity and CVD risk, informing primordial prevention strategies during pregnancy.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Tirzepatide-induced pneumatosis intestinalis: a rare but clinically significant gastrointestinal adverse effect.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists such as tirzepatide are increasingly prescribed to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity because they improve glycemic control and promote weight loss. Although gastrointestinal adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, constipation, and delayed gastric emptying are well recognized, very rare cases of pneumatosis intestinalis have also been reported in association with this class of medications. We report the first documented histologic diagnosis of a possible tirzepatide-associated pneumatosis intestinalis. A 55-year-old man with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and obstructive sleep apnea underwent colonoscopy for evaluation of abdominal pain, constipation, and anal fissures. He had been receiving tirzepatide therapy for approximately 1 year and experienced a 49-pound weight loss. Colonoscopy demonstrated mucosal edema of the cecum and ascending colon. Biopsy specimens of the colon revealed mucosal and submucosal air-filled spaces associated with foreign body-type giant cell reactions and mixed inflammatory infiltrates, including eosinophils and neutrophils, consistent with pneumatosis intestinalis. The patient lacked other recognized risk factors for pneumatosis intestinalis, and his symptoms improved following discontinuation of tirzepatide. As the use of tirzepatide and related glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists continues to increase, awareness of this rare side effect and its characteristic histologic features should facilitate prompt recognition and accurate diagnosis. Reporting these rare events remains essential to refine the safety profile of these increasingly used medications and improve our understanding of their long-term gastrointestinal effects in broader patient populations.

papers.title: Jue Tone Music Therapy for Post-stroke Depression in China: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effects of Jue tone music therapy on depressive symptoms, sleep quality, activities of daily living, and selected serum biomarkers in patients with post-stroke depression (PSD).MethodsIn this randomized controlled trial, patients with PSD were randomly assigned to a control group or an intervention group. The control group received usual care, including sertraline hydrochloride and comprehensive rehabilitation training. The intervention group received additional Jue tone music therapy based on Five Element Music Therapy for 6 weeks. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 24-item Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD-24) and the depression subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS-D). Sleep quality and activities of daily living were evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Barthel Index (BI). Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) levels were measured before and after the intervention.ResultsA total of 91 patients completed the study (control group, n = 46; intervention group, n = 45). After 6 weeks, the intervention group showed significantly lower HAMD-24, HADS-D, and PSQI scores and higher BI scores compared with the control group (all P < 0.01). Serum IL-6 levels were significantly reduced, while BDNF and 5-HT levels were significantly increased in the intervention group (all P < 0.05). No significant differences in adverse events were observed between groups.ConclusionJue tone music therapy is a safe and effective adjunct to usual care, improving depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and functional outcomes in patients with PSD.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine

papers.title: Cognitive Performance and Adherence to Treatment in Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment is common in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but how cognition relates to positive airway pressure (PAP) adherence among asymptomatic referrals is less clear. We evaluated whether global cognition using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) is associated with continuous PAP (CPAP) adherence. In total, 29 OSA patients underwent the MoCA test. Data on CPAP adherence was obtained at 3 months. The Pearson correlations quantified associations between MoCA scores and adherence/effectiveness measures. The mean age of the participants was of 64.3 ± 8.0 years, and 51.7% of them had MoCA scores < 26. Among those with mild OSA, who scored 5 to 15 on the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), 57.1% were impaired despite being asymptomatic by history. Higher MoCA correlated with higher CPAP use (r = 0.65, p = 0.023) and showed a positive trend with nights used > 4 hours (r = 0.54, p = 0.073). The attention domain correlated with both average hours/day and percent nights > 4 hours, while lower language scores correlated with higher residual AHI (r = -0.69, p = 0.019). The high prevalence of cognitive impairment despite the absence of self-reported symptoms suggests that cognitive deficits may be underrecognized in patients undergoing evaluation for OSA. The association of global cognition and attention with CPAP use further suggests that cognitive function may influence patients' ability to successfully engage with treatment. Cognitive impairment was present in 51.7% of this asymptomatic cohort and in 57.1% of participants with mild OSA. Higher global MoCA and attention scores were associated with greater CPAP use, while lower language scores were associated with higher residual AHI.

papers.title: The Interplay of Child Sleep Disturbances, Maternal Burnout, and Marital Quality in Iranian Mothers.
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationships between child sleep disturbances, maternal burnout, and marital quality among Iranian mothers. Using a cross-sectional design, data were collected from 564 married mothers of preschool-aged children (aged 5-6 years) through validated questionnaires: the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire , the Parental Burnout Assessment , and the Quality of Marriage Index . A structural equation model (SEM) was used to test hypothesized associations among the variables. The final model demonstrated excellent fit to the data. Results indicated a significant positive correlation between child sleep disturbances and maternal burnout ( r = 0.374, p < 0.001) and significant negative correlations between maternal burnout and marital quality ( r = -0.368, p < 0.001) and between child sleep disturbances and marital quality ( r = -0.217, p < 0.001). In the measurement model, strong indicators were identified for each latent variable, including night wakings (β = 0.683) and parasomnias (β = 0.533) for child sleep disturbances, and contrast with the previous maternal self (β = 0.909) and emotional exhaustion (β = 0.864) for maternal burnout. These findings advance theoretical understanding by highlighting key interconnections between child sleep, maternal well-being, and relational outcomes within a specific cultural context. The results underscore the importance of a systemic approach in examining how child sleep disturbances and maternal burnout jointly relate to marital quality, with implications for family well-being interventions.

papers.title: Exploring the Link Between Inflammatory Gene Variants and Phenotypes of Periodontal Disease and Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Periodontal disease (PD) and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are prevalent chronic inflammatory conditions affecting over 50% of Colombians and a substantial proportion of the global population. This study investigated genetic associations between interleukin (IL) gene variants (IL-1β, IL-10, IL-17) and the risk of PD, OSA, or their coexistence in 129 Colombian individuals, including cases (PD, OSA, PD + OSA) and healthy controls. Genotyping was performed using PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing. Key findings revealed that IL-1β variants (rs1143627, rs16944) significantly increased OSA risk (OR = 3.6 and 3.36; p = 0.004 and 0.008). The IL-10 (rs1800896) also elevated OSA risk (OR = 4.44; p = 0.004), whereas the IL-17 (rs2275913) showed a protective effect (OR = 0.21; p = 0.0003). Among individuals with PD + OSA, IL-1β variants (rs1143627, rs16944) conferred an even higher risk (OR = 4.8; p = 0.0007-0.0008). No significant genetic associations were found for PD alone. In conclusion, these findings highlight the central role of inflammation in PD-OSA comorbidity, driven by dysregulated interleukin signaling pathways. Variants in IL-1β and IL-10 may predispose individuals to both conditions, suggesting shared inflammatory mechanisms. These insights could inform the development of targeted therapies addressing inflammatory pathways underlying PD and OSA. The study underscores the importance of genetic and molecular research in advancing personalized treatment strategies for overlapping chronic diseases.

papers.title: searchMECFS: An online, interactive platform to facilitate secondary use of biospecimens and associated research data from myalgic encephalomyelitis studies.
papers.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex, debilitating disease affecting multiple body systems, with no established biomarkers for diagnosis or treatment. This publication introduces searchMECFS, a free, interactive online platform developed by the Data Management and Coordinating Center (DMCC) of the ME/CFS Research Network, with funding from the National Institutes of Health. The platform's purpose is to facilitate the secondary use of biospecimens and associated research data from ME/CFS clinical studies by improving accessibility, visibility, and sharing of these resources. Currently, searchMECFS facilitates access to biospecimens and associated data from two studies: The Chronic Fatigue Initiative (CFI) study funded by the Hutchins Family Foundation and the Multi-Site Clinical Assessment of ME/CFS study (MCAM) funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Users can query participant demographics and clinical information and request available biospecimens through an application process. Eight specimen types are currently available, although availability varies by study. The results highlight a case where a researcher used the searchMECFS platform to identify 40 serum samples, which contributed to published research on circadian rhythm disruption in ME/CFS. searchMECFS aims to accelerate scientific discovery within the ME/CFS research community by improving biospecimen utilization, fostering data sharing, and supporting collaboration.

papers.title: Insomnia Symptoms in Doctor of Pharmacy Students in the United States: A Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a common sleep disorder that can negatively affect academic performance, mental health, and quality of life. Despite the rigor of Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) training, little is known about the prevalence of insomnia among PharmD students in the United States. This study evaluated the presence of insomnia across multiple institutions and characterized symptoms to inform targeted interventions. This is a cross-sectional, institutional review board-exempt survey of pharmacy students at nine schools in the United States between March and April 2025. Participants completed demographic information and the Insomnia Symptom Questionnaire (ISQ), a validated 13-item instrument designed to detect insomnia. The primary outcome was the proportion of students meeting ISQ criteria for symptoms consistent with insomnia. Secondary outcomes included characterization of insomnia-related symptoms and comparisons by year in training. Descriptive statistics and chi-squared tests were applied. Seventy-three students completed the survey (mean age 25.5 years; 59% female; 74% Asian American). Overall, 26% met criteria for symptoms consistent with insomnia, with the highest prevalence among first-year (35%) and fourth-year (27.3%) students. Fatigue was the most common symptom, reported by 53.4% of students, followed by daytime sleepiness (38.3%) and concentration difficulties (37%). Difficulty staying asleep and frequent awakenings were less often endorsed. Approximately one in four PharmD students screened positive for symptoms consistent with insomnia, with fatigue and difficulty concentrating as prominent features. These findings highlight a potential need for wellness initiatives and targeted interventions to support sleep health in pharmacy education.

papers.title: Caregiver-Reported Behavioral Changes After Donepezil Transdermal Patch Therapy in Alzheimer's Disease: An Exploratory Real-World Network Analysis.
papers.abstract: To characterize caregiver-reported behavioral changes after donepezil transdermal patch therapy and to examine the descriptive connectivity of co-occurring improvements in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD). This retrospective, single-center observational study included 26 patients meeting the 2011 National Institute on Aging-Alzheimer's Association criteria for probable AD dementia. Approximately 2-4 months after patch initiation, caregivers rated nine behavioral domains using routine, non-validated single-item change assessments as improved, unchanged, or worsened relative to the pre-treatment state. A descriptive co-improvement network was used solely to summarize pairwise co-occurrence of binary improvement indicators using phi-coefficients and observed strength centrality. Because of the small sample and sparse binary events, all network measures were treated as sample-specific descriptive quantities rather than inferential estimates. The most frequently improved domains were smiling/positive affect (12/26, 46.2%), calmness (9/26, 34.6%), and night-time sleep (8/26, 30.8%). Calmness had the highest observed strength centrality (2.467), followed by grooming behavior (2.059), hobbies/interests (2.009), and housework/instrumental activities of daily living (1.938). Calmness remained the highest-strength node in all 26 leave-one-participant-out sensitivity analyses. No treatment discontinuations or serious adverse events were documented. Caregiver-perceived calmness, assessed as a single non-validated change item, was the most highly connected domain in this small descriptive co-improvement network. The findings are exploratory and do not establish treatment efficacy, a validated agitation-related outcome, temporal direction, or mechanism. Prospective studies using standardized behavioral measures are needed.
keywords: behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia

papers.title: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Two Novel Variants in the GJB1 Gene.
papers.abstract: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease X-linked Type 1 (CMTX1), caused by GJB1 mutations, presents diagnostic challenges due to phenotypic heterogeneity and novel variants. This study reviews clinical data from 2021-2024 and investigates the mechanisms of two novel GJB1 variants. We retrospectively analyzed eight male patients, evaluating clinical signs, electrophysiology, and sural nerve biopsies. Pathogenicity of novel variants was assessed via bioinformatics, ChimeraX molecular modeling, and HeLa cell models focusing on protein localization and channel function (scratch-loading/DAPI assays). Patients showed typical distal muscle atrophy and intermediate conduction velocities; three exhibited rare CNS white matter abnormalities. Two novel variants were identified: c.130dupT and c.124A > G. c.130dupT led to a complete "loss of expression" of the full-length Cx32 protein. c.124A > G resulted in significant cytoplasmic protein retention (p < 0.05). Molecular modeling revealed a physical constriction (1.229 Å) in the channel bottleneck and an increased electrostatic barrier. Functional assays confirmed significant impairment in both gap junction and hemichannel activity (p < 0.01). This study identifies two previously unreported GJB1 variants and elucidates their distinct pathogenic mechanisms: c.130dupT acts through loss of expression, whereas c.124A > G causes functional defect via structural channel constriction. These findings expand the genetic spectrum of CMTX1 and provide a basis for precise molecular diagnosis.

papers.title: Mandibular Advancement Devices With Remote Monitoring Technologies: Expanding the Dentist's Role in the Management of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent disorder with significant systemic and quality-of-life consequences. Mandibular advancement devices (MADs) are an established treatment option, but conventional follow-up often relies on intermittent visits and self-reported adherence. Sensor-integrated MADs and remote monitoring may enable objective adherence assessment and personalized longitudinal care, although their additional clinical value remains uncertain. This narrative review critically appraises current evidence on sensor-integrated MADs with remote monitoring for OSA, focusing on treatment adherence, objective monitoring, personalized therapy, and dentists' evolving role in longitudinal multidisciplinary care. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library through 2025 for English-language studies on MADs, sensor-integrated oral appliances, and remote monitoring in OSA. We synthesized evidence across six domains spanning pathophysiology, clinical practice, and digital innovation. The evidence indicates that MADs improve respiratory and patient-reported outcomes, while integrating sensor-based and remote monitoring technologies offers additional opportunities for objective assessment of adherence and nightly appliance use. Remote monitoring and feedback may improve the consistency of MAD use, although increases in total nightly wearing time have not been consistently demonstrated. Emerging smart MADs can also monitor parameters such as sleep duration, sleep position, and respiratory events, while adaptive systems may enable individualized adjustment of mandibular advancement. However, current evidence does not yet establish that smart MADs provide superior long-term physiological, cardiovascular, or patient-reported outcomes compared with conventional MAD therapy. Smart MADs may nonetheless strengthen adherence assessment, expand the dentist's role in longitudinal care, and support personalized, multidisciplinary OSA management; further clinical validation and standardized long-term studies are needed to determine their incremental therapeutic value.

papers.title: Plasma Proteomic Landscape of Multidimensional Sleep Health and Its Association With Depression Risk Under Genetic Susceptibility.
papers.abstract: Multidimensional sleep health, encompassing duration, snoring, chronotype, insomnia symptoms, and daytime sleepiness, is associated with various chronic diseases. However, its relationship with depression risk, especially the underlying molecular mechanisms across different levels of genetic susceptibility, remains unclear. In this prospective cohort study, we analyzed data from 36,852 UK Biobank participants, integrating multidimensional sleep scores, plasma proteomic data covering 2,911 proteins, and polygenic risk scores (PRS) for depression. Sleep-related proteins were identified via elastic net regression, and their associations with incident depression were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Mediation and interaction analyses were conducted to explore the role of proteomic features and their effect modification by genetic risk. Seventy-three plasma proteins were selected by elastic net as sleep-related proteomic features, mainly involving immune regulation, neural signaling, metabolic homeostasis, and extracellular matrix remodeling. The proteomic score derived from these features was positively correlated with sleep health (r = 0.234, p < 1×10-100). Healthy sleepers had a lower risk of depression (HR = 0.553, 95% CI: 0.454-0.674, p < 0.001), as did those with higher proteomic scores (HR = 0.660, 95% CI: 0.566-0.770, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis suggested that the proteomic signature statistically accounted for a modest proportion of the observed association between sleep health and incident depression. A significant additive interaction was observed between unhealthy sleep and high genetic risk (RERI = 0.280, 95% CI: 0.022-0.538). This study characterizes the plasma proteomic profile of multidimensional sleep health and identifies sleep-associated proteomic signatures related to incident depression across levels of genetic susceptibility. These findings highlight potential biological pathways for further investigation and require independent replication and causal validation before clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Nonlesional Extratemporal Epilepsy Surgery Using Subdural Grid Implantation.
papers.abstract: Nonlesional extratemporal lobe epilepsy (ETE) remains one of the most challenging forms of drug-resistant epilepsy to treat surgically because seizure onset zones are often poorly defined on conventional neuroimaging. The long-term effectiveness of subdural grid-guided surgery in this population remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate long-term surgical outcomes in patients with intractable nonlesional extratemporal epilepsy who underwent subdural grid-guided epilepsy surgery. A retrospective study was conducted from January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2024. Clinical, pathological, and invasive electroencephalography data were reviewed. Seizure outcomes were assessed using Engel's classification at 6 months and 2 years after surgery. Fifty-five patients with nonlesional extratemporal epilepsy were included. Seizure freedom (Engel class I) was achieved in 12 patients (21.8%) at 6 months and increased to 30 patients (54.5%) at 2 years. These improvements were not statistically significant ( p = 0.16 and 0.53, respectively). Favorable trends toward better seizure outcomes were observed in patients aged from adolescence to middle adulthood, those with tumor pathology, and those with parietal lobe seizure foci. Subdural grid-guided surgery for nonlesional extratemporal epilepsy resulted in seizure-free rates of 21.8% at 6 months and 54.5% at 2 years, with improvement over time but without statistically significant predictors of outcome.

papers.title: C-Reactive Protein as a Predictor of Cardiovascular Events and Mortality in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Propensity-Matched Analysis Using the TriNetX Research Network.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) increases cardiovascular disease risk through systemic inflammation, particularly through elevated C-reactive protein (CRP). This study investigated whether CRP stratification predicts mortality and cardiovascular events in OSA patients. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis using the TriNetX Research Network, encompassing electronic health records from 130 healthcare institutions. Adults (ages 18-90 years) with OSA were stratified by CRP concentration: elevated (≥ 3.0 mg/L) versus low (≤ 2.9 mg/L). After propensity score matching for demographics and comorbidities, 240,727 participants per cohort were followed for five years. Primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included cardiovascular events, arrhythmias, and acute kidney injury. Elevated CRP was associated with significantly higher all-cause mortality (11.3% versus 7.0%; HR 1.695, 95% CI 1.662-1.727; p < 0.001). The elevated CRP group demonstrated heightened cardiovascular risk: cardiogenic shock (1.0% versus 0.5%; HR 2.003), heart failure (9.8% versus 6.5%; HR 1.594), pulmonary hypertension (4.9% versus 3.4%; HR 1.508), and acute kidney injury (11.0% versus 6.4%; HR 1.825), all p < 0.001. Arrhythmic complications were also increased: atrial fibrillation/flutter (6.3% versus 4.8%; HR 1.372) and ventricular tachycardia (2.3% versus 1.8%; HR 1.388), both p < 0.001. Elevated CRP constitutes a robust predictor of mortality and cardiovascular morbidity in OSA populations. Assessment of inflammatory biomarkers may enhance risk stratification, informing intensified monitoring and targeted therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: Acute Onset of Suicidal Ideation after Starting Lemborexant in a Patient with a Mood Disorder.
papers.abstract: A 24-year-old woman with treatment-resistant depressive symptoms and chronic insomnia developed acute, intrusive suicidal ideation with intent on day 5 after starting lemborexant 10 mg nightly. Emergency assessment did not identify intoxication, metabolic disturbance, psychosis, mania, akathisia, or other acute precipitants. Pretreatment polysomnography showed severe insomnia with a sleep efficiency of 14.5% and absent REM sleep, without sleep-disordered breathing. Lemborexant was discontinued immediately, and suicidal ideation resolved completely within 24 hours without additional pharmacological intervention. The Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale yielded a score of 6, consistent with a probable adverse drug reaction. At 6-month follow-up, the patient remained free of suicidal ideation with sustained functional stability. This case adds clinically relevant documentation to pharmacovigilance concerns about potential suicidality with dual orexin receptor antagonists and supports structured suicide risk assessment and early follow-up when initiating these agents in patients with mood disorders.

papers.title: Intragastric Balloon Versus Sleeve Gastrectomy: Baseline Characteristics and Comorbidity Prevalence in a Nigerian Cohort.
papers.abstract: Data describing baseline demographics, clinical characteristics, and obesity-related comorbidities among patients seeking bariatric interventions in Sub-Saharan Africa are limited. We describe demographics, obesity class, procedure selection, and comorbidity prevalence among patients undergoing intragastric balloon (IGB) or sleeve gastrectomy (SG) at a private center in Nigeria. Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected electronic records for adults (≥18 years) who underwent IGB (n = 113) or SG (n = 55) between January 2023 and January 2025 was performed. Data on demographics, anthropometrics, obesity class, and comorbidities were extracted. Group comparisons used χ 2 for categorical and t-tests or Mann-Whitney U for continuous variables; with the significance set at P < 0.05. A total of 168 patients (92.3% female) were included; mean age 35.4 ± 9.4 years. SG patients presented with higher mean body mass index (SG: 43.1 ± 6.8; IGB: 39.3 ± 7.9 kg/m2; P = 0.003) and weight (SG: 122.8 ± 19.9 kg; IGB: 111.7 ± 26.0 kg; P = 0.006). Higher obesity classes (IV-V) were more frequent in SG (38.2% combined) than IGB (18.5% combined; P = 0.013). Overall, 47.0% had ≥1 comorbidity; the prevalence was higher in SG (56.4% vs 42.5%; P = 0.09). Hypertension was the most common comorbidity (28.6%), and male patients (n = 13) carried a disproportionate comorbidity burden (≥1 comorbidity 84.6% vs 43.9% in females; P = 0.01) and had a higher prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnoea. Bariatric interventions in Nigeria are predominantly sought by younger women. Patients opting for SG had significantly greater obesity severity and tended towards higher comorbidity rates. Men were underrepresented but had markedly higher comorbidity burden when presenting for care. These findings highlight gender disparities, procedure selection patterns, and the need for broader awareness and access to metabolic and bariatric services in Nigeria.
papers.journal: Journal of the West African College of Surgeons

papers.title: Current review of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists and risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.
papers.abstract: Emerging data has identified a potential association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a typically sudden, painless, and irreversible cause of optic nerve-mediated vision loss. This review synthesizes the current clinical, epidemiologic, and potential mechanism linking GLP-1RA-based therapies to NAION risk, informing balanced risk assessment and interdisciplinary clinical decision-making. A structured PubMed search was performed using terms including "GLP-1 receptor agonist," "semaglutide," "liraglutide," "tirzepatide," and "nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy," in addition to NAION risk factors, including disc-at-risk anatomy, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, renal disease, and ischemic heart disease. A small cup-to-disc ratio ("disc-at-risk") was found to be the most robust anatomical predictor of NAION. Systemic microvascular disease (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia) and conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea and end-stage renal disease were also linked to increased susceptibility to optic nerve head ischemia. Although data across electronic health records, national registries, and pharmacovigilance analyses suggest a very low absolute incidence of NAION, the use of GLP-1RAs demonstrates a statistically significant association with NAION development, yielding relative risk estimates between 1.2 and 4.3. At this time, the potential association between GLP-1RA therapy and NAION should be interpreted as a safety signal rather than a contraindication. Screening for disc-at-risk anatomy, consideration of prior NAION history, and patient counseling regarding acute visual symptoms may be warranted prior to initiation of therapy. As evidence evolves, collaboration between endocrinologists and ophthalmologists will be essential to support safe and effective patient care.

papers.title: Depression severity and sleep efficiency's associations with amyloid burden are additive but dependent on underlying genetic risk in late life depression.
papers.abstract: Evidence linking late-life depression (LLD) to amyloid beta (Aβ) burden remains mixed, possibly in part due to limited examinations of the confounding role of comorbid sleep disturbance and the moderating role of the apolipoprotein E (APOE) ɛ4 gene. We analyzed 110 older adults (ages 65-88, 66% female) with LLD to jointly model depression severity and sleep disturbance's relationship with Aβ, and to examine the moderating role of APOE ɛ4 genotype. Depression severity, sleep efficiency, and sleep duration did not demonstrate a direct relationship with Aβ; however, a significant APOE ɛ4 moderation effect occurred for depression severity and sleep efficiency. In APOE ɛ4 carriers only, higher depression severity and lower sleep efficiency were associated with greater total Aβ burden and indicated greater likelihood of reaching clinical cutoffs for amyloid positivity. The effects of depressive symptoms and sleep efficiency were statistically unique and additive. Exploratory analyses demonstrated APOE ɛ4 also moderated the effect of lifetime duration of untreated depression on increased Aβ. Depression severity and sleep efficiency's relationship with Aβ may be dependent on the presence of the APOE ɛ4 allele. This, among other individual differences, may partially explain mixed findings examining LLD as a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. Furthermore, these findings do not suggest that the relationship between depression severity and amyloid is explained by the confounding role of sleep duration or sleep efficiency.

papers.title: Intrinsic circadian organization of the spinal cord and dorsal root ganglia.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms coordinate daily fluctuations in physiology and behavior, yet their organization within primary sensory pathways remains poorly defined. Although somatosensory responsiveness varies across the day-night cycle, it is unclear whether peripheral sensory circuits possess molecular mechanisms for temporal regulation. To determine whether the spinal-peripheral sensory axis harbors intrinsic circadian clocks and to define the molecular scope and functional organization of circadian regulation in dorsal root ganglia (DRGs). We used real-time bioluminescence imaging to assess circadian oscillations of the core clock protein PER2 in the spinal dorsal horn and DRGs. To characterize molecular regulation, we performed RNA sequencing across a 52-hour circadian time course in DRGs. We demonstrate that the spinal dorsal horn and DRGs harbor robust, tissue-autonomous circadian clocks, with sustained PER2 oscillations. Circadian analysis identified 626 rhythmic genes (3.6% of expressed genes) in DRGs, with nonuniform phase distributions forming discrete temporal clusters. Functional annotation revealed phase-specific enrichment of processes including transport, neuronal structure, and proteostasis, suggesting coordinated temporal deployment of distinct molecular programs rather than uniform oscillations. Cross-referencing with neuropathic pain-associated genes revealed limited overlap; however, overlapping genes aligned to specific baseline phase windows enriched for regenerative annotations. Potassium channel-related signaling components implicated in neuropathic pain also showed baseline circadian modulation. These findings establish the spinal dorsal horn and DRGs as intrinsically circadian tissues and reveal a temporally structured molecular landscape in DRG, providing a framework for understanding how peripheral sensory processing, plasticity, and homeostatic regulation are coordinated across the day-night cycle.

papers.title: Remimazolam ED95 for Preoperative Sedation in Children with Obstructive Sleep Apnea, with Obesity or a Reference-Range BMI: A Biased-Coin Dose-Finding Study.
papers.abstract: Obesity may alter total-body-weight dosing of remimazolam, whereas obstructive sleep apnea narrows the respiratory safety margin. We estimated the ED95 for protocol-defined preoperative sedation in children with obesity or a reference-range body mass index (BMI). In this prospective, single-center sequential dose-finding study, 80 children aged 3-17 years with a clinical OSA diagnosis undergoing adenoidectomy and/or tonsillectomy entered study-defined obesity (BMI-for-age >95th percentile) or reference-BMI (25th-84th percentile) groups (40 each). Independent biased-coin sequences used total-body-weight doses, starting at 0.20 mg/kg with 0.05 mg/kg steps. The response was a Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) score ≥4 at 3 minutes after completion of a 1-minute intravenous bolus. Isotonic regression and 2000 bootstrap resamples yielded ED95 estimates and bias-corrected percentile 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Responses occurred in 35/40 (87.5%) participants in the obesity group and 34/40 (85.0%) in the reference-BMI group. ED95 estimates were 0.38 mg/kg (95% CI, 0.32-0.39) and 0.44 mg/kg (95% CI, 0.39-0.44), respectively. The difference was -0.05 mg/kg (95% CI, -0.13 to 0.05). During 15-minute observation, one child per group developed hypoxemia (SpO2 93%) that resolved after a jaw-thrust maneuver. One reference-BMI participant developed bradycardia (50 beats/min), which responded to atropine. No child had a ≥30% decrease in mean arterial pressure. The protocol-specific ED95 values of a 1-min remimazolam bolus for RSS ≥4 at 3 min were 0.38 mg/kg in children with obesity and 0.44 mg/kg in children with a reference-range BMI.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota-Immune-Inflammation Axis as a Putative Pathogenic Axis in Chronic Insomnia: Mechanistic Dissection of NLRP3 Inflammasome and NF-κB Signaling.
papers.abstract: Chronic insomnia represents one of the most prevalent sleep disorders worldwide, yet current symptomatic treatments largely fail to target its root pathophysiology. Moving beyond conventional neurocentric frameworks, converging evidence positions gut microbiota dysbiosis as a potential upstream contributor to insomnia via the microbiota-gut-brain axis, with immune-inflammatory cascades serving as proposed mediating pathway. Mechanistically, disrupted gut microbial communities compromise intestinal mucosal barrier integrity, enabling lipopolysaccharide translocation that activates TLR4-mediated NF-κB signaling. This triggers systemic low-grade inflammation, marked by elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17 and TNF-α, reduced anti-inflammatory IL-4 and IL-10, and Th17/Treg immune imbalance. Centrally, circulating inflammatory signals activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, driving caspase‑1‑dependent pyroptosis and a pro‑inflammatory microglial activation state (conventionally described as "M1‑like" polarization), which disrupts sleep-wake neural circuitry and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis homeostasis. Dysregulated PI3K/Akt signaling and aberrant microbial metabolites-including depleted short-chain fatty acids and a pathological shift in tryptophan metabolism toward the neurotoxic kynurenine pathway-further amplify the vicious cycle between sleep disturbance and neuroinflammation. This review systematically maps the full pathological cascade from intestinal dysbiosis to central insomnia phenotypes, and compares translational strategies including psychobiotic strains, fecal microbiota transplantation, dietary intervention and traditional Chinese medicine formulas targeting this axis. Collectively, this work proposes an integrated microbiota-immune-sleep regulatory framework, offering novel mechanistic insights and microbiome-based therapeutic avenues for precision insomnia management.

papers.title: The Association Between Tuberculosis-Related Stigma and Sleep Quality Among Hospitalized Tuberculosis Patients: The Indirect Role of Anxiety.
papers.abstract: To investigate the relationship between perceived stigma and sleep quality among hospitalized tuberculosis patients, and to examine the indirect role of anxiety in this relationship. A cross-sectional study design was employed. A convenience sample of 2179 tuberculosis patients was selected and assessed using the TB-Related Stigma Scale (TSS), the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The indirect effect of anxiety was examined using the PROCESS macro (Model 4; Hayes, 2018) with 5000 bootstrap resamples to generate 95% bias-corrected confidence intervals for indirect effects. Perceived stigma was positively associated with PSQI scores (r = 0.143, p < 0.01), indicating that higher perceived stigma was associated with poorer sleep quality. Perceived stigma was also positively correlated with anxiety (r = 0.180, p < 0.01), and anxiety was positively associated with PSQI scores (r = 0.446, p < 0.01), suggesting that higher anxiety was also associated with poorer sleep quality. Perceived stigma was indirectly associated with sleep quality through anxiety. These findings suggest that perceived stigma and anxiety may be potential contributing factors related to sleep quality in this population. Given the cross-sectional design, they should be interpreted as hypotheses-generating rather than evidence of causal intervention effects; future intervention studies may consider combined approaches-such as cognitive behavioral therapy together with social support and anxiety-management interventions-to examine whether targeting perceived stigma and anxiety improves sleep outcomes.

papers.title: Physical Activity and Cognitive Function in Postmenpausal Women: Depressive Symptoms and Sleep Disorder as Sequential Mediators.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to examine the association between physical activity (PA) and cognitive function in postmenopausal women, and to investigate whether depressive symptoms and sleep disorder act as sequential mediators of this association. We analyzed 5614 postmenopausal women in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2018). PA was grouped into quartiles (Q1-Q4), with total cognitive score as the primary outcome. Mixed-effects models with restricted cubic splines characterized dose-response relationships. A multilevel serial mediation model with bias-corrected bootstrapping (1000 resamples) estimated indirect effects, and a cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) evaluated longitudinal directionality. PA showed an inverted U-shaped association with cognition and a U-shaped association with depressive symptoms. Relative to Q1, moderate PA (Q2) was associated with higher cognitive scores (β = 0.559; 95% CI, 0.232-0.887), whereas the highest stratum (Q4, reflecting heavy physical labor) was associated with lower scores (β = -0.354; 95% CI, -0.697 to -0.010). In Q2, significant indirect effects were observed through depressive symptoms (a1×b1 = 0.053), abnormal sleep duration (a2×b2= 0.078), and the serial depression-to-sleep pathway (a1×d×b2 = 0.006), totaling 0.137 (95% CI, 0.083-0.201). In the CLPM, moderate PA predicted fewer subsequent depressive symptoms (β = -0.056) and better cognition (β = 0.039), consistent with the mediation results. In postmenopausal women, moderate PA is associated with better cognitive function, partly through fewer depressive symptoms and improved sleep, whereas high-intensity physical labor is associated with poorer cognition. Depressive symptoms and sleep may therefore be relevant considerations when planning strategies to preserve cognitive health in this population.

papers.title: The EEG multi-scale brain network and high-order synergy changes in disorders of consciousness during general anesthesia.
papers.abstract: Brain network alterations during general anesthesia (GA) have been extensively investigated in individuals with intact consciousness. However, network dynamics in patients with disorders of consciousness (DoC) under anesthetic perturbation remain poorly understood. We recorded electroencephalogram (EEG) signals from 33 DoC patients (16 UWS and 17 MCS) during GA across three states (DoC-Resting, DoC-MOSSA, and DoC-Recovery). A multi-scale brain network framework was proposed. Low-order network characteristics were assessed using unbiased minimum spanning tree (MST) and directed phase lag index (dPLI), while high-order organization was evaluated using topological data analysis (TDA) and high-order mutual information (HO-MI). UWS patients exhibited a fragmented, line-like topological backbone with lower leaf fraction (p < 0.05) and tree hierarchy (p < 0.05) than MCS patients. dPLI analysis revealed impaired prefrontal top-down directional communication in UWS patients, whereas MCS patients showed transient disruption and recovery of frontoparietal directional organization during anesthesia. Under anesthesia, TDA revealed reduced H1 maximum Betti number in UWS patients (p < 0.01), indicating impaired topological resilience, while MCS patients showed relatively preserved network organization. Furthermore, HO-MI analysis showed increased total correlation with redundant information processing in UWS patients during anesthesia, whereas MCS patients restored synergistic information integration within the central-parietal network during recovery. GA reveals distinct scale-dependent network alterations between MCS and UWS patients. Persistent impairment of directed communication and high-order synergistic integration characterizes disrupted network organization in UWS. The proposed multi-scale EEG framework integrating MST, dPLI, TDA, and HO-MI provides candidate network biomarkers for perioperative consciousness monitoring and assessment in DoC patients. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s11571-026-10567-4.

papers.title: Time-of-day effects of acute and regular exercise on sleep quality and mood: a three-level meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Evidence regarding whether exercise timing differentially affects sleep quality and mood remains inconsistent. This study examined the effects of acute and regular exercise performed at different times of day on sleep and mood. Eight English and Chinese databases were searched from inception to June 2026. Parallel and crossover randomized trials were synthesized using three-level meta-analysis with non-diagonal sampling variance-covariance matrices. Exercise vs. Control and direct Time vs. Time comparisons were analyzed separately, with CR2 cluster-robust inference used as a robustness check. Thirteen studies contributed 81 effect sizes (40 sleep and 41 mood). For sleep, Exercise vs. Control showed a large effect in the conventional model (g = 0.86, 95% CI [0.26, 1.46], p = 0.005), but CR2 inference was non-significant (p = 0.109). Direct Time vs. Time comparisons were non-significant (g = 0.15, 95% CI [-0.08, 0.39], p = 0.209; CR2 p = 0.127), with no stable advantage for morning, afternoon, or evening exercise. For mood, Exercise vs. Control was large but non-significant (g = 0.95, p = 0.056). Time vs. Time was significant conventionally (g = 0.30, p = 0.027) but not under CR2 inference (p = 0.097). Afternoon vs. Evening favored afternoon exercise (g = 0.50, p = 0.001), although based on only two studies. Exercise itself may be more important than its specific timing for sleep, whereas mood may show timing-related signals that remain insufficiently robust for definitive recommendations. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier [CRD420261431622].

papers.title: An evidence-informed occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation of aquanauts in underwater habitats: a scenario-based framework development study.
papers.abstract: Underwater habitats represent emerging extreme workplaces in which pressure exposure, immersion, confined living, external underwater tasks, and delayed access to definitive care create combined occupational health and safety demands. Candidate selection establishes baseline suitability. It cannot, on its own, specify which preventive and response capabilities should be taught, practiced, and documented between selection and deployment. We developed a scenario-based, evidence-informed occupational health curriculum for the pre-deployment preparation of non-medical research personnel. The design case was deliberately narrow. It placed three to six crew members in a 15-m habitat for 14 days, with topside telemedical support and limited immediate specialist care. Peer-reviewed studies and official manuals were mapped to mission phases, occupational and operational risk events, expected actor actions, and feasible non-medical performance. No Delphi round or validation study was undertaken. Internal project documents only defined the scenario. The occupational health curriculum specification contains four domains, ten modules, and 28 observable learning outcomes. Emergency preparedness, physical self-maintenance, psychological and team functioning, and underwater operational safety are separated by immediate performance purpose. Together, the domains connect worker protection across routine prevention, acute response, psychosocial risk management, and task-specific safety. Three modules carry the psychological and team content. Sleep and circadian management, emotional self-regulation, and crew communication with conflict management are each specified on their own. This article offers a preliminary occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation that underwater habitat programs can adapt. It is evidence-informed and unvalidated. The framework addresses worker protection within a bounded underwater workplace while preserving the authority of diving, clinical, and mission-governance systems. Independent stakeholder review, instructor usability testing, pilot training, and analog-mission observation remain necessary before the framework informs any operational readiness decision.

papers.title: Comorbid insomnia and sleep apnea (COMISA) and incident cardiovascular risk: a prospective analysis from the HypnoLaus cohort.
papers.abstract: Comorbid insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea (COMISA) is a prevalent and clinically relevant phenotype. While both insomnia and OSA have been individually associated with increased cardiovascular risk, few longitudinal studies have evaluated their combined impact on incident cardiovascular events in the general population. A total of 1860 participants from the CoLaus|PsyCoLaus cohort, originally recruited between 2003 and 2008 and assessed in the HypnoLaus study between 2009 and 2013, were included, all of whom underwent full-night polysomnography and completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). OSA was defined as an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15 events/h. Insomnia symptoms were defined as difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep ≥3 times/week over the past month. Participants were classified into four groups: reference (no insomnia, no OSA), insomnia alone, OSA alone, and COMISA. Incident cardiovascular events (coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death) were adjudicated by an expert committee over a median follow-up period of 7.92 years [IQR: 6.30-8.77]. Cox regression models were adjusted for demographic, behavioral, and clinical covariates. Compared to the reference group, COMISA was independently associated with an increased risk of incident cardiovascular events (HR 1.78, 95% CI: 1.09-2.92, p = 0.021), while no significant association was observed for insomnia (HR 0.59, 95% CI: 0.31-1.11, p = 0.10) or OSA alone (HR 1.33, 95% CI: 0.84-2.10, p = 0.22). A significant interaction between OSA and insomnia was observed (p = 0.035). Results were consistent in participants without prior cardiovascular events and across alternative definitions of COMISA. COMISA, but not OSA or insomnia alone, was associated with increased incident cardiovascular events. These findings highlight the need to identify and treat COMISA as a distinct and high-risk phenotype in cardiovascular prevention strategies. Faculty of Biology and Medicine of Lausanne, Lausanne University Hospital, Swiss National Science Foundation, Leenaards Foundation, GlaxoSmithKline, Ligue Pulmonaire Vaudoise.

papers.title: Chronic pain in narcolepsy reflects interacting neurobiological and psychological mechanisms: a mini-review.
papers.abstract: Chronic pain prevalence is increased in the sleep disorder narcolepsy, but the underlying reason for this remains debated. This mini review summarizes and discusses current evidence on links between narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) and type 2 (NT2) and chronic pain, exploring whether pain is best understood as a consequence of the pathophysiology or secondary to its manifestations and comorbidities. Registry-based and self-reported data indicate a high prevalence of chronic pain in NT1, while objective pain tests show inconsistent differences between NT1 and healthy individuals. This discrepancy suggests involvement of secondary mechanisms not readily captured by experimental pain testing. Comparable pain prevalence in NT1 and NT2 also speaks against orexin deficiency as a sole driver of chronic pain in NT1. Alternatively, altered dopaminergic signaling downstream of orexin could be a shared contributor to pain in NT1 and other fatigue-related conditions. Finally, the presence of activating autoantibodies in NT1 suggests a possible immune-mediated component for some patients. Overall, chronic pain is highly prevalent in both NT1 and NT2. It likely arises from a combination of neurobiological and psychological factors, with immune mechanisms as a possible additional contributor, rather than, in NT1, orexin dysfunction alone. This perspective highlights the clinical need for more holistic treatment approaches and for future studies with improved case-control matching, larger NT1 samples, especially among patients with chronic pain, and more detailed comparisons with NT2.

papers.title: PRNP D178N-129MM prion disease: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease-like cortical ribboning without prominent early insomnia.
papers.abstract: The PRNP p.Asp178Asn (D178N) mutation on a methionine-bearing codon-129 allele is classically associated with fatal familial insomnia (FFI), but some carriers develop a Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)-like phenotype. We report a 59-year-old woman with two months of rapidly progressive cognitive-language decline, caregiver-observed nocturnal sitting-up and sleep talking, weight loss, extensive cortical diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) ribboning, positive cerebrospinal fluid 14-3-3, and positive multisite skin real-time quaking-induced conversion. Electroencephalography showed diffuse slowing without periodic sharp-wave complexes. PRNP sequencing identified D178N with methionine homozygosity at codon 129. A focused literature review identified six previously reported individual D178N-129MM cases with prion-compatible cortical or cortical-striatal DWI abnormalities. Because these reports were selectively ascertained by imaging and used heterogeneous clinical assessments, they were not treated as a clinical series or compared numerically with MRI-negative cohorts. Other D178N-129MM reports show normal DWI in non-insomnia cognitive or motor presentations, objective sleep abnormalities preceding insomnia, and occasional cortical DWI hyperintensity in FFI cohorts. D178N-129MM disease shows substantial phenotypic and imaging heterogeneity. Marked CJD-like cortical ribboning can occur in an initially non-sleep-dominant presentation and should not exclude an FFI-associated genotype. MRI pattern alone should not be used to infer a specific clinical phenotype; PRNP sequencing and objective sleep assessment remain important when clinically appropriate.

papers.title: Melatonin supplementation in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review of clinical, imaging, biomarker, and safety outcomes.
papers.abstract: Melatonin may act on immune, oxidative, and circadian pathways relevant to multiple sclerosis (MS), yet its clinical benefits and safety profile remain unclear. This systematic review assessed the efficacy and safety of oral melatonin supplementation in adults with MS. We searched MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception through August 15, 2026, and included randomized and prospective non-randomized intervention studies. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. Given substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, we synthesized findings without meta-analysis, following SWiM guidance, and rated certainty of evidence with GRADE. We registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251167112). We included 10 independent studies, reported across 17 publications, covering 435 participants. Nine were randomized trials (two of them crossover designs), and one was a prospective non-randomized intervention study. Melatonin doses spanned 0.5-300 mg/day, with treatment durations from 2 weeks to 14 months. The evidence did not show reductions in relapse activity, disability progression, or new MRI activity. Small studies suggested possible improvements in sleep, fatigue, pain, physical function, cognition, mood, autonomic function, body composition, and inflammatory, metabolic, or oxidative-stress biomarkers, but these results were inconsistent and rarely replicated. Doses of 0.5-25 mg/day were generally well tolerated, though some participants discontinued treatment and adverse-event reporting remained incomplete. At 300 mg/day, three of four melatonin-treated participants developed hypertransaminasemia, which resolved after withdrawal and recurred on rechallenge in one case. Certainty of evidence was low or very low for every outcome assessed. Current evidence does not support a disease-modifying effect of melatonin in MS. Any symptomatic or biomarker benefits need confirmation in larger, well-designed trials, and high-dose melatonin may carry meaningful hepatic risk.

papers.title: Working Time Exposures and Occupational Injury Among Delivery Gig Workers in China: Indirect Pathways Through Sleep Quality.
papers.abstract: Delivery gig workers face elevated risks of occupational injury, yet little is known about how working time exposures contribute to injury risk and the pathways underlying this association. This study examined the associations between multiple dimensions of working time exposures and occupational injury and whether sleep quality represented an indirect pathway co-occurring with these associations. Using cross-sectional survey data from 1,537 delivery gig workers in Shanghai, China, we examined the associations between three dimensions of working time exposures (daily working hours, weekly working days, and night-shift frequency) and occupational injury. Sleep quality was examined as a potential indirect pathway based on the Effort-Recovery Model. We estimated a series of regression models and used bootstrap methods to decompose direct and indirect associations while adjusting for sociodemographic and job-related covariates. Longer daily working hours and more frequent night shifts were directly associated with higher occupational injury counts. Weekly working days and night-shift frequency showed significant indirect associations with occupational injury through poorer sleep quality. Robustness checks using a binary injury indicator yielded consistent results. Working time exposures are associated with occupational injury risk among delivery gig workers through both direct exposure-related associations and indirect pathways involving sleep quality. Interventions and policies targeting excessive working hours, night work, and sleep quality may help reduce injury risks in this vulnerable transport workforce.

papers.title: Associations Between Weekly Commute Time, Weekday Sleep Duration, and Driving Fatigue Among Working Adults in Israel.
papers.abstract: Long commutes are recognized as an occupational health risk and road safety risk. In high-traffic countries, prolonged commuting may represent a potentially significant yet underexplored public health concern, particularly with respect to gender-specific vulnerability patterns. This study thus examines the association between weekly commute time, weekday sleep duration, and driving fatigue via a gender-based analysis. Data relating to 3,387 employed adults were drawn from the 2023 Israel Social Survey. Long commuting was defined as ≥15 hours/week; 20.2% of the survey respondents were long commuters, 54.7% were women, and 45.3% were men. Outcomes measured included insufficient sleep duration (<6.5 hours) and self-reported driving fatigue. Multivariable logistic regression models were stratified by gender and adjusted for demographic and work-related variables. Long commuting was linked to insufficient sleep duration [odds ratio (OR) = 1.56] and increased driving fatigue (OR = 1.71) among women and with driving fatigue (OR = 2.13) but not significantly with sleep duration among men. Health behaviors differed according to gender, with women with long commutes engaging in more physical activity (46.2% vs. 40.3%) and exhibiting lower obesity rates (18.1% vs. 19.3%) and men being less active, more obese, and smoking more frequently. Extended weekly commuting appears to be an independent gender-specific occupational health risk factor, exerting effects on sleep, fatigue, and health behaviors. Women report more sleep disruption, while men experience higher fatigue and adverse health behaviors. These findings highlight the need for gender-sensitive health interventions, flexible work policies, improved transportation infrastructure, and recognition of commuting as an important modifiable determinant of worker health.

papers.title: Comparative effectiveness of traditional Chinese medicine treatment strategies for insomnia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Insomnia causes daytime impairment and reduced quality of life. We evaluated the comparative efficacy and safety of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) treatment strategies for insomnia. Nine databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, SinoMed) were searched through January 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Primary outcomes were ISI and PSQI scores; secondary outcomes included clinical efficacy and adverse events (AEs). Data were synthesized using frequentist network meta-analysis. Twelve RCTs involving 1,260 participants were included, evaluating five strategy nodes: TCM alone, TCM plus Western medicine (WM), WM alone, placebo, and CBT-I. For ISI, TCM plus WM ranked highest (SUCRA 89.7%) and significantly improved scores versus placebo (OR 2.84, 95% CI 1.42-5.68) and WM (OR 1.96, 95% CI 1.08-3.56). For PSQI, TCM plus WM showed the highest probability of improvement (SUCRA 71.9%) with greater reduction versus placebo (MD -2.31, 95% CI -3.65 to -0.97). For clinical efficacy, SUCRA values were 86.6% for TCM plus WM, 77.2% for TCM, 20.9% for WM, and 15.3% for placebo. For AEs (higher SUCRA indicating better safety), SUCRA values were 94.8% for WM, 43.9% for TCM plus WM, 31.1% for placebo, and 30.2% for TCM. Sensitivity analysis excluding secondary insomnia confirmed robust findings. Integrated TCM-WM and TCM therapies demonstrate clinical efficacy and acceptable safety for insomnia management. The review protocol was prospectively registered in the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (INPLASY) (Registration number: INPLASY202680041; DOI: 10.37766/inplasy2026.8.0041).

papers.title: Non-motor correlates of anxiety in de novo Parkinson's disease: a cross-sectional study with exploratory subgroup analyses.
papers.abstract: Anxiety is a prevalent early non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), but its clinical correlates remain poorly defined in de novo, drug-naïve patients. This retrospective cross-sectional study enrolled 284 medication-naïve de novo PD patients and 147 age- and sex-matched healthy controls to identify non-motor correlates of anxiety after adjustment for demographic and motor covariates, and explore potential subgroup heterogeneity. Anxiety was assessed with the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale; multivariate logistic regression and prespecified stratified analyses by age, sex, disease duration, Hoehn-Yahr stage and motor severity were performed. Clinically significant anxiety was detected in 44.0% of PD patients versus 8.1% of controls (p < 0.001), with psychic anxiety as the dominant subtype. After multivariate adjustment, higher depressive symptom scores were positively associated with anxiety (OR = 1.386), whereas better sleep quality (OR = 0.965) and intact olfactory identification (OR = 0.815) were negatively associated with anxiety; motor severity showed no significant association after multivariable adjustment. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed heterogeneous patterns of sleep and olfactory correlates across clinical strata. The three-factor predictive model yielded an overall classification accuracy of 84.81%. These findings indicate that non-motor abnormalities, rather than motor impairment, are associated with anxiety in early PD after adjustment for demographic and motor covariates. The distinct correlative patterns across subgroups provide preliminary clinical clues for the heterogeneous neurodegenerative processes underlying PD-related anxiety, and support routine screening of depressive, sleep and olfactory symptoms to facilitate anxiety risk stratification at initial diagnosis.

papers.title: Prefrontal EEG Delta-Beta Coupling Marks Depressed State in Adult Siblings.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is marked by disorganization in electrophysiological brain networks, yet it remains unclear whether such disorganization reflects the state-dependent pathological effects or a trait-like vulnerability. We analyzed resting-state electroencephalographic (EEG) delta-beta phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) in two sibling cohorts. Current-MDD families included individuals with current MDD and their currently unaffected siblings (n=36), and remitted-MDD families comprised individuals with remitted MDD and their lifetime unaffected siblings (n=110). Delta-beta high PAC was significantly elevated (p corr ≤0.05) over the left-medial frontal region in participants with current MDD relative to their unaffected siblings. In the remitted-MDD families, no significant differences were observed. Regrouping all individuals irrespective of family ties into current MDD, remitted MDD, and never-depressed controls confirmed significantly elevated frontal delta-beta high PAC at rest in the current-MDD subgroup compared to other subgroups. Overall, delta-beta high coupling reflects the depressive state rather than a trait-like or familial vulnerability.
